title: Gold Market Commentary: Go with the flow
gist: World Gold Council says gold fell 8.5% in September to US$4,176/oz on higher yields and dollar plus futures liquidation, while UK ETF flows far exceeded model-predicted levels, suggesting rising term premia and fiscal concerns are driving a sustained shift.

insights.claim: Gold finished September at US$4,176/oz, down 8.5% m/m and 4.4% y-t-d, versus a record high of US$5,405 on 29 January 2026.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold sits about 23% below its January peak.

insights.claim: The US 10-year yield climbed 53bps to 5.3% and the DXY rose 2% in September, major contributors to gold's drop in the Gold Return Attribution Model.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Real-rate and dollar strength remain gold's main near-term headwinds.

insights.claim: Net managed money COMEX positions fell US$12bn (84t) and spreading positions fell US$22bn (156t) in September, diverging from US$10bn of ETF inflows.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Futures liquidation, not ETF selling, drove the price decline.

insights.claim: UK gold ETFs attracted 54t in Q3 versus about 18t predicted by a five-year relationship with Western flows, leaving a 36t excess even though UK funds are only about one-third of Western gold ETF assets.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: UK demand is extraordinary relative to history.

insights.claim: Since July, excess UK gold ETF flows have moved with the UK term premium, a relationship that was weak earlier, suggesting inflation or fiscal worries and risk that the Bank of England is behind the curve are driving demand.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold demand is linked to gilt fiscal-risk premia; sample is short.

insights.claim: Unlike the short-lived 2022 gilt crisis, the current yield rise is global and ETF demand looks like a sustained shift; the OBR's July report warned the UK fiscal path is unsustainable without significant tightening.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Fiscal-credibility stress is a medium-term gold support.

insights.claim: Rising yields and term premia in France and Germany suggest similar fiscal concern, though ETF inflows there have been less pronounced.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Watch Eurozone term premia as a leading gold demand signal.

insights.claim: If bond yields stay elevated despite lower Fed, BoE and ECB tightening expectations, investors are focused on fiscal and term-premium risk rather than policy rates, which would keep supporting gold demand.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Yield behavior after a dovish repricing is the test for the gold-fiscal thesis.
insights.locator: In summary: what to watch in October
